metadata.goal: Investigate how taxi movement patterns vary across weather and temperature conditions at different times of day.
metadata.header: Porto Taxi Speed under Rain and Temperature Conditions
metadata.dataset_description: A constructed set of 180 weekday Porto taxi trips linked to archived hourly Porto weather observations from February–April 2014. GPS paths follow the local OSM road graph; the tables support speed comparisons by weather, temperature, time period, route length, and central-area exposure.

insights: During weekday daytime periods, trips observed in rainy conditions have lower average speeds than trips observed in dry conditions.
The speed difference between rainy and dry conditions is most pronounced during the afternoon, while the difference becomes much smaller during late-night hours.
Within dry daytime periods, average trip speeds differ only moderately between cooler and warmer conditions compared with the larger difference observed between rainy and dry periods.
A small group of rainy-period trips remains relatively fast; these trips are mainly longer trajectories that spend less of their routes in the central area.
summary: Rain is associated with lower weekday daytime taxi speeds, especially in the afternoon, while the late-night weather gap is small. Temperature differences within dry daytime periods are more moderate. A small fast-rain exception group consists mainly of longer, less centrally exposed routes.
